title: The Moebius function lands on a carrier without negatives as a pair of Nat-valued halves whose sum is its absolute value and whose product is zero
statement: The Moebius function takes values in {-1, 0, 1} and the natural numbers have no negatives, so mu is declared as two Nat-valued functions: moebiusPos n is 1 exactly when mu(n) = +1 and moebiusNeg n is 1 exactly when mu(n) = -1, each 0 unless n is squarefree. Two theorems make the pair behave as one signed quantity: their sum is the absolute value of mu(n), and their product is 0, so at most one half is nonzero. Both are proved by the three-way case split the definitions make -- not squarefree; squarefree with an even number of prime factors; squarefree with an odd number.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.moebius_pos_add_neg : ((x0 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (AxNat.add (AxNat.moebiusPos x0) (AxNat.moebiusNeg x0)) (AxNat.moebiusAbs x0))
formal.kernel_statement: Nat.omegaCount n := Nat.Multiset.card (Nat.factorization n); Nat.moebiusAbs n := bool_select_nat (Squarefree n) 1 0; Nat.moebiusPos n := bool_select_nat (Squarefree n) (bool_select_nat (Nat.beq (Nat.mod (omegaCount n) 2) 0) 1 0) 0; Nat.moebiusNeg n := bool_select_nat (Squarefree n) (bool_select_nat (Nat.beq (Nat.mod (omegaCount n) 2) 0) 0 1) 0. The companion law is Nat.moebius_pos_mul_neg : forall n, Eq (mul (moebiusPos n) (moebiusNeg n)) zero. Squarefree is at the BARE root namespace, not Nat.squarefree.

provenance.established_by: axeyum lane `arithmetic-functions`, roadmap item W2-18: `nat_prelude/arith_functions_family.rs`. ADR-1619, following ADR-0603's graded-statement-family shape.
provenance.source: The Moebius function, standard since 1832. What is not standard is the encoding: a classical development gives mu a signed codomain and never faces this question.

prior_art.establishes: the same function with a signed codomain; the graded-pair encoding here exists because the divisor aggregate this family is built on is Nat-valued and no Int-valued range-sum toolkit exists in the tree

evidence.supports: the pair really encodes mu, with the sign convention the right way round
evidence.notes: mu(1) = +1, mu(2) = -1, mu(3) = -1, mu(4) = 0, mu(5) = -1, mu(6) = +1, each read off both halves and off moebiusAbs, with every value reduced by the kernel. The parity-flipped definition has exactly the same type and would swap the n = 2 and n = 6 rows, so those two instances are what separate the readings. Magnitudes stay at or below 6 because every Nat numeral in this kernel is unary and both Squarefree and Nat.factorization are fuel-bounded searches.
evidence.checker_paired_negative: moebiusPos 2 is asserted NOT to reduce to 1 (the parity-flipped answer) and moebiusAbs 4 NOT to reduce to 1 (the answer a definition ignoring squarefreeness would give).

evidence.supports: the two halves carry exactly the absolute value of mu between them
checkers: Kernel::add_declaration (re-derives the type from the proof term)
evidence.notes: Instantiated at n = 6 (squarefree, even omega), n = 2 (squarefree, odd omega) and n = 4 (not squarefree) -- all three branches of the proof's own case split, so no branch is confirmed only by the other two.
evidence.checker_paired_negative: The companion law Nat.moebius_pos_mul_neg is instantiated at the same three arguments. A pair where BOTH halves were 1 would satisfy neither law, and a pair where both were always 0 would satisfy the product law but fail the sum law at n = 6.

notes: This fact records an ENCODING decision as much as a theorem. It does NOT include Moebius inversion, or even the summatory identity that mu(d) summed over the divisors of n is [n = 1] -- see F:nat-dirichlet-convolution-commutes for why that did not land. Nat.omegaCount counts prime factors WITH multiplicity (Omega, not omega); the two agree exactly on the squarefree numbers, which is the only place these definitions read it, so the choice is invisible to mu.
